title: Exact Möbius–Lambert and foreign-residue coordinates for the totient tail

concepts.label: absolute Lambert-pair regrouping
concepts.note: A product-filtered, positive-index regrouping justified by absolute summability for x in the half-open unit interval.

concepts.label: literal totient-tail coordinates
concepts.note: Exact shifted Möbius-pulse and positive-index foreign-residue representations of the literal tail.

concepts.label: divisor and foreign residue channels
concepts.note: The finite divisor-channel shadow and the complete positive-index foreign-residue kernel are kept distinct.

concepts.label: renormalized Lambert center
concepts.note: Exact agreement between residue-projection and Lambert-projection coordinates once the cutoff is at least twice the height.

concepts.label: reduced numerator-gap consumer
concepts.note: A conditional target-miss theorem whose substantive input is a rational numerator gap larger than the denominator-scaled analytic complement.

concepts.label: representation versus separation boundary
concepts.note: Exact coordinate identities do not themselves prove positivity, noncancellation, rational separation, cofinal escape, or irrationality.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Let w,v : ℕ → ℝ satisfy |w(d)| ≤ d and |v(m)| ≤ m at positive indices, let P be any decidable predicate on ℕ, and let 0 ≤ x < 1. Then the absolutely convergent positive-pair sum of w(d)v(m)x^(dm), restricted by P(dm), equals the positive-index sum whose nth coefficient is the divisor sum ∑_{e∣n} w(e)v(n/e), restricted by P(n).
statement_nodes.engine: Absolute summability of the polynomially bounded Lambert pair family, transport across the positive-pair/product-fibre equivalence, and a sigma antidiagonal regrouping.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The analytic rearrangement principle is classical; the project-specific value is the exact positive-index and arbitrary-product-filter interface used by the totient-tail formalization.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: This is an exact real-series regrouping on 0 ≤ x < 1. It does not cover x=1, assert positivity of either weight, or imply integrality, irrationality, or target avoidance.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For every N, the literal tail totientTail(N) is exactly the convergent sum over positive d of the shifted Möbius pulse μ(d)·2^(d-r_d(N))·((⌊N/d⌋+1)/(2^d-1) + 1/(2^d-1)^2), where r_d(N)=d-(N mod d).
statement_nodes.engine: Apply the product-filtered Lambert regrouping to the strict-tail predicate N<n, identify each divisor fibre by its first multiple strictly beyond N, and simplify the resulting geometric series.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: This is a project-specific exact bridge recorded in the paper and Lean source; no external priority or novelty claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The equality is an exact coordinate formula, not a sign or noncancellation result. It neither proves the tail nonzero nor yields integrality, irrationality, or target avoidance by itself.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For every N, totientTail(N) is exactly the convergent sum over positive d of positiveForeignResidueKernel(d,N).
statement_nodes.engine: Rewrite the literal tail as its shifted Möbius pulse sum and use the pointwise equality between the positive-index foreign-residue kernel and the shifted pulse term.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The theorem is the formal project's global representation bridge; no historical novelty claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Here “positive” describes the positive-natural index type, not the sign of the summand: the kernel contains a Möbius factor and is not asserted nonnegative. The identity alone gives no separation, nonvanishing, irrationality, or target-miss theorem.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For every positive height H, scaleExplicitShadow(H) equals the finite sum of residueIncrement(d,H) over the positive divisors d of H.
statement_nodes.engine: Use the rational divisor-sum formula for the scaled Möbius shadow, cast it to the ambient real expression, and identify each divisor-channel residue increment termwise.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The finite divisor-channel identity is a project-specific normalization; no standalone novelty claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: This identifies only the divisor-indexed residue channels. It does not identify the full infinite foreign-residue tail and does not supply a separation or target-miss conclusion.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For every H>0 and every cutoff D with 2H≤D, renormalizedResidueProjection(H,D) equals lambertProjectedDiagonal(H,D). Equivalently, the explicit divisor shadow, projected foreign defect, and rational first-tail correction combine exactly into the canonical Lambert projected center.
statement_nodes.engine: Split the finite residue projection into divisor and foreign channels, replace the divisor channels by the explicit shadow, use the global positive-index kernel formula for the literal tail, and reconcile the remaining tail terms with the Lambert projected diagonal.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: This closes a project-internal representation obligation under an explicit cutoff; no external novelty claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The cutoff condition is part of the theorem. Coordinate agreement is not rational separation: this theorem does not provide a numerator gap, bound the analytic complement, prove target avoidance, or establish irrationality.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Fix H,D and a natural m. If the reduced numerator of lambertProjectedDiagonalRat(H,D) stays at distance at least m from every integer multiple of its reduced denominator, and the Lambert square-complement bound multiplied by that denominator is strictly less than m, then ScaleFullTargetHit(H) is false.
open_antecedents: Produce a natural m that uniformly separates the reduced numerator of lambertProjectedDiagonalRat(H,D) from every integer multiple of its reduced denominator.
Prove that the Lambert square-complement bound at H,D, after multiplication by that reduced denominator, is strictly smaller than m.
statement_nodes.engine: Scale the reduced rational numerator separation by the positive denominator, convert it to a real separation from every integer, and invoke the existing projected-center separation criterion for failure of the full target hit.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The deduction from a certified rational gap and a smaller analytic error is a standard separation argument; the substantive open work lies in producing the hypotheses at useful heights.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: This consumer does not construct m, prove the uniform numerator gap, establish the analytic bound, produce a cofinal family of heights, or imply irrationality; its conclusion concerns one fixed height H.

declaration_roles.routing_basis: The paper's exact shifted-tail route explicitly factors through this product-filtered Lambert regrouping.
The paper displays the exact pulse formula and the Lean theorem proves it for the literal tail.
The paper inventory identifies this exact global foreign-residue bridge, and the Lean theorem proves the displayed equality.
The paper and theorem identify the finite divisor residue channels with the explicit Möbius shadow.
The exact theorem bounds the paper table's shorthand to coordinate agreement for H>0 and 2H≤D.
The paper's numerator-gap route and exact Lean theorem make this the separation consumer downstream of the coordinate layer.

intra_zone_relations.basis: The shifted-pulse theorem applies the generic restricted Lambert regrouping to the strict-tail predicate and then evaluates the divisor fibres.
The foreign-residue theorem rewrites the shifted-pulse sum pointwise through positiveForeignResidueKernel_eq_shiftedMobiusPulseTerm.
The finite shadow identity controls the divisor-indexed residue channels, while the global kernel identity controls the complete positive-index tail coordinate.
The agreement proof uses the global foreign-residue kernel identity as its exact infinite-tail representation input, together with additional tail identities.
The agreement proof replaces the divisor part of the finite residue split by scaleExplicitShadow using this exact identity, alongside other tail inputs.
Coordinate agreement identifies the residue and Lambert centers; the numerator-gap theorem is a distinct conditional separation consumer and must not be conflated with that agreement.
